lateEvents.description: Events in this project that arrived later than this endpoint's window, before the endpoint's filter and scope are applied, recorded in the whole arrival hours from `since`: the first hour boundary at or after the later of the endpoint's last window change and 30 days ago (the delivery log retention). It counts arrivals, so it includes late events since removed by retention or deletion and can exceed what a search finds. The count is approximate: it is exact in normal operation, but after a storage failure, a retried write or a restore it can be lower or higher than the true number. There is no backfill: arrivals before the deployment added this count are not included. Do not use it for reconciliation. 0 when the window is null. null only in a PATCH response when the count could not be read: the settings were saved regardless; read the endpoint again for the count.

200.description: Versioned CSV/JSONL or complete original-payload JSONL (jsonl-evidence; 422 masked_export for masked scopes), limited to the caller scope. CSV columns: id, timestamp, action, outcome, description, project_id, received_at, environment, category, severity, actor_type, actor_id, actor_name, actor_email, impersonator_id, impersonator_name, executor_type, executor_id, executor_name, job_id, job_attempt, tenant_id, tenant_name, source, targets, changes, context, attributes, conformance, schema_version, sdk, schemaVersion. There is no trailer: a complete download is one that ends normally (a non-empty file ends with a newline; an export with no matching events is an empty JSONL body or a CSV header only); a failure after the headers aborts the connection, so treat any transport error as an incomplete file and discard it. Audited in workspace activity as export.requested, then export.completed or export.failed (actor = the API key; metadata.access names the key, tenant and viewer token). See docs/exports.md.

403.description: scope_exceeded: the requested scope is wider than the key scope. forbidden: the credential is a viewer token, which can never mint (use a read key).

429.description: a request budget is exhausted (the project bucket; for viewer tokens the minting key + tenant bucket; for minting the per-key bucket) or the peer authentication-failure budget is. Public limits fail open if Redis is unavailable.
